home.heroLede: A Vietnamese American parade krewe for Greater Sacramento
home.definition: A coordinated Vietnamese American parade presence for Greater Sacramento — groups marching together as a krewe. From past parade efforts, we grow toward a prestigious parade corps.
home.kreweBody: In New Orleans Mardi Gras tradition, a krewe is a social club that organizes to parade together — shared identity, costumes, and presence on the route. We borrow that idea: Vietnamese American groups showing up as a coordinated train at civic parades across Greater Sacramento.

chapters.headline: A parade we used to host
chapters.body: In 2010, neighbors marched Tết down Stockton Blvd on Little Saigon’s designation weekend. Two years later came a community-hosted Little Saigon Tết parade. Lunar New Year Tết 2026 tried to host one again, but it showed how thin Vietnamese American parading had become.

chapters.headline: A professionally run parade corps
chapters.body: Little Saigon Krewe is the effort to make parading amazing again. Imagine winning awards. Getting recognition. Inspiring every generation to come.

history.headline: Parade history
history.lead: The community has put Tết parades on the street. Vietnamese groups have also marched as a unit on someone else’s route — the train Little Saigon Krewe is building. Newest years first.

host-2010.headline: Little Saigon designation — and a New Year parade
host-2010.body: City and County ribbon cuttings, and a Tết parade down Stockton Blvd toward Florin. Neighbors filled the corridor that designation weekend — we marched in Little Saigon.

host-2012.headline: Little Saigon Street Festival Parade
host-2012.body: The corridor filled again — GSVACC, Florin Partnership, and many amateur cameras. Rain moved the weekend from January 21 to this Saturday. LITTLE SAIGON TV taped it; it remains the best-recorded Little Saigon Tết parade we have.

host-2013.headline: Xuân Quý Tỵ Parade
host-2013.body: A corridor parade and hội chợ on Stockton Blvd / Florin after the branded weekend. HyRo taped the street parade that Saturday.

host-2014.headline: Giáp Ngọ Parade
host-2014.body: VACOS hosted parade and hội chợ at NE Florin & Stockton Blvd (rain-moved). SBTN taped both the march and the lot.

host-2016.headline: Little Saigon Tet Parade + Lunar Flower Festival
host-2016.body: Parade at 9 AM, Stockton Blvd & Fruitridge — the same Saturday as the lot festival. HeuFamilyEnt taped the march; KCRA named both hosts.

host-2017.headline: Đinh Dậu Parade
host-2017.body: The street march landed on Tết Saturday, from the Happy Garden lot along Stockton Blvd into the hội chợ. SN&R also billed a Florin & Stockton Blvd fair Saturday–Sunday, February 4–5 — a later weekend, not this tape.

pitch.headline: Check in on 10th by 10:45. March 11:00–12:30 as a train.
pitch.body: On Golden Harvest morning, each group checks in at the Golden Harvest desk on 10th St in front of the Capitol between 9:00 and 10:45 AM, then lines up on 10th St (vehicles stage on 9th). Meet & greet and a group photo happen during staging. Then we march 11:00 AM–12:30 PM as a train of krewe groups, one after another. Festival runs 10:00 AM–4:30 PM on the west side of the Capitol. We are your front door to Golden Harvest: one place for questions. Each group still registers under its own name.

portal.headline: Participant waivers
portal.body: Every marcher needs a participant waiver — adults consent for themselves; parents or guardians consent for minors. Officers sign in, register the club, and share the join link. It includes Golden Harvest’s 2026 Waiver and Release Form, so one signature covers both — we pass the signed waivers to Golden Harvest.
portal.cutoff: Digital waivers due Friday, October 23, 2026. Any late waivers must be printed and brought in person Saturday morning.

timeline.headline: How we get ready
timeline.intro: Stay with Little Saigon Krewe for questions — we’ll batch anything Golden Harvest needs so your club doesn’t have to chase two organizations. Soft interest first; paperwork comes in later gates.

steps.when: Now — catch-up if you missed Aug 28
steps.title: Soft commit — interest
steps.body: The Aug 28 interest gate has passed — still email. Name an officer/parade contact and a rough headcount. Interest and contacts only — not final paperwork.

steps.title: Participant waivers — every marcher
steps.body: Every marcher needs a participant waiver on portal.cpalss.com — adults consent for themselves; parents or guardians sign for high schoolers and other minors. Officers register the club and share the join link. It includes Golden Harvest’s 2026 Waiver and Release Form, so marchers sign once and we pass the waivers to Golden Harvest. Digital due Fri Oct 23, 2026 — late waivers must be printed and brought Saturday morning.

steps.title: Golden Harvest unit registration
steps.body: Each group still files its own Golden Harvest registration form and emails it to the parade coordinators (their emails are at the bottom of the form). Download the blank copy below — “LSK A team” is already filled in under Additional Information. Golden Harvest’s 2026 guidelines set marching groups at 20–300 people; the form still prints the older 15-person minimum, so go by 20. Tell us your headcount and we’ll combine smaller groups so everyone clears 20. We batch questions to the coordinators.

steps.title: Pick your sign carrier
steps.body: Golden Harvest provides every team a team name sign, so banners are optional — Golden Harvest doesn’t provide banners, but you’re welcome to bring your own. Name one person to carry the team sign at the front of your group and return it to the registration desk after the parade. There’s no separate Golden Harvest waiver to file — the cPALSs Portal waiver is Golden Harvest’s 2026 Waiver and Release Form.

steps.title: Block order inside Little Saigon
steps.body: We work with Golden Harvest on the order of krewe groups in our parade train — based on who has actually filed.

steps.title: Parade day
steps.body: Check in at the Golden Harvest desk on 10th St in front of the Capitol between 9:00 and 10:45 AM with your sign carrier. Meet & greet is Little Saigon Krewe’s staging window — also the group-photo opportunity — facilitated by tribe champions. Parade hours are 11:00 AM–12:30 PM. Expected weather for 9:00 AM–1:00 PM: sunny and clear, about 54°F at 9 AM warming to around 64°F by 11 AM and ~70°F by 1 PM (forecast as of Oct 23). Staging details in Transit below.

faq.q: Should I register through the Golden Harvest site?
faq.a: No — register through Little Saigon Krewe first. Clubs can register with Golden Harvest on their own. Golden Harvest’s 2026 guidelines ask for at least 20 people per marching group (300 max), and parade registration is due Tuesday, October 20, 2026. Our job is to combine smaller groups so the combined headcount meets that minimum.

faq.q: Do we file Golden Harvest’s waiver separately?
faq.a: No. The cPALSs Portal waiver is Golden Harvest’s 2026 Waiver and Release Form, so each marcher signs once — adults for themselves, parents or guardians for high schoolers and other minors — digitally by Friday, October 23. Any late waivers must be printed and brought in person Saturday morning. We pass the signed waivers to Golden Harvest. The one other thing Golden Harvest needs from every team is a sign carrier: one person who carries the Golden Harvest team name sign at the front of your group and returns it to the registration desk after the parade.

No. Groups arrange their own ride — drive, carpool, or take SacRT on their own. Little Saigon Krewe is not running a bus or a staffed light-rail escort. SacRT is free on parade day, though: print or screenshot Golden Harvest’s free-ride flyer (linked under Transit) and show it to the bus operator or light-rail fare inspector. It’s good Saturday, October 24, 9:00 AM–6:30 PM, and one flyer covers a group traveling together.

No — performing is optional. Many groups simply march behind their Golden Harvest team sign. If you do want to perform, there are two different options: a short performance during the parade, or a longer main-stage slot at the festival afterward. See the next question.

faq.q: What’s the difference between a parade performance and a stage performance?
faq.aHtml:
Parade performance — during the march. Once your group passes the start line, you can dance or perform as you go. Each group gets one stop, in front of the parade stage, for 1 minute at most — any longer and the groups behind you get stuck. Don’t stop elsewhere on the route for photos; take group photos during staging.

Stage performance — a separate 5–10 minute slot on the festival main stage after the parade, for groups Golden Harvest selects. The stage is 24 × 36 ft at ground level on rubber mats, not a raised riser. To be considered, check Stage Performance on the Golden Harvest registration form and fill in performance type, number of performers, and program length. Stage registration is due Thursday, October 1, 2026.

faq.a: No. Golden Harvest does not provide changing rooms. Plan to arrive dress-ready. There is space on Capitol Mall for practice and warm-up before step-off.

No required uniform, but Golden Harvest requires apparel suitable for all ages. The parade is televised, so dress in a way that shows your club or group identity (colors, shirts, a banner if you have one, traditional wear if you like). Costume OK; traditional optional. Mornings can be a bit chilly — bring a light jacket for check-in and staging. We don’t have lockers to store jackets once we start marching, so arrange for someone to look after them.

faq.q: What’s not allowed in the parade?
faq.a: Golden Harvest’s rules: no sharp equipment, fireworks, or anything that could hurt someone. Don’t throw anything along the route. No inappropriate language or behavior. Floats, vehicles, and trailers must be under 40 ft long, 10 ft wide, and 13.5 ft tall, be insured, and have licensed drivers. Motorcycle groups need at least 10 motorcycles. Groups that don’t follow the guidelines can be removed from the parade.

No — banners are optional. Golden Harvest gives every group a team name sign, and that sign leads your group on the route. Pick one person to carry it at the front of your group and return it to the registration desk after the parade. If your club already has a banner, you’re welcome to bring it too.

transit.headline: Getting there
transit.intro: This year families drive, carpool, or take transit on their own. Little Saigon Krewe is not running a chartered bus or a staffed light-rail escort. SacRT buses and light rail are free on parade day with Golden Harvest’s free-ride flyer (link below).
transit.pathTitle: SacRT Blue Line — free on parade day with the flyer (not a krewe escort)
transit.parkingLead: Carpools are encouraged. Two options: metered street parking (you must pop in or refeed every 2 hours), or flat-rate Golden Harvest event parking on ParkWhiz — lots typically run $10–$15. Street meters take coins, credit cards, and mobile-app payments.
transit.parkingRates: Typical event rates: $10–$15 · prices vary by lot

steps: Print or screenshot Golden Harvest’s free-ride flyer. One flyer covers a group traveling together — show it to the bus operator when you board, or to a fare inspector on light rail.
Take a SacRT Elk Grove local bus toward Cosumnes River College (CRC) — the southern end of the Blue Line.
Board Blue Line light rail toward Watt / I-80 (downtown direction).
Exit at 8th & Capitol Station. Walking groups: two blocks east to check-in on 10th St in front of the Capitol. Vehicles: one block east to 9th St.
Return: board Blue Line at 8th & Capitol toward Cosumnes River College (check the headsign), then Elk Grove bus home.
notes: The free-ride flyer is good Saturday, October 24, 9:00 AM–6:30 PM on SacRT buses and light rail. Leave early enough to reach check-in by 10:45 AM.
Saturday schedules differ from weekday rush-hour — Elk Grove weekday-only commuter buses (e.g. E13) won’t help parade morning. Use local EG routes + Blue Line, and verify times the week before.
Light rail uses one-way streets downtown; your outbound stop and return stop may differ.
Florin / South Sacramento riders can often skip the Elk Grove bus leg and board Blue Line closer to home.

champions.headline: Meet & Greet
champions.body: We’re rallying different organizations and clubs into tribes — high school with high school, college with college, and so on — so peers meet peers before we march. Staging is also the group-photo window. Each tribe has a champion who helps facilitate those connections: they hold the tribe sign and open the conversation.

fund.headline: Fund the Krewe
fund.body: Cover breakfast, gas, water, or a banner so students and clubs can march. Cash check to cPALSs (memo LSK 2026) or in-kind that matches the gift. Ask which slots are still open before you commit.
